learning_outcomes.description: Formulate a significant and novel research question in or across the fields of doctrinal law, legal theory or socio-legal studies.
Design a research project to investigate that question using appropriate approaches to legal research and methodologies.
Utilise legal writing techniques that are appropriate to different academic aims and audiences.
Manage research projects to produce quality work within time-constraints.

assessments.task_description:
Students will submit a Research Proposal of no more than 2,000 words comprising a detailed description of the research project and a draft outline of the proposed research paper. The research proposal should:

  • demonstrate scholarly ability to identify relevant resources and to summarise and categorise existing knowledge;
  • identify the ‘gap’ in the knowledge that your project is attempting to address;
  • position your project in the context of existing knowledge; and
  • clearly identify the aims, scope and boundaries of your project.

There is no single correct way to write a research proposal. Supervisors and students will discuss the format for the research proposal and draft outline.

Any material in excess of the word count will be disregarded by the marker. The research proposal should include footnotes and bibliography. However, the footnotes and bibliography are not included in the word count. Footnotes should be limited to reference citations. Any substantive discussion in a footnote will be disregarded by the marker. (For the avoidance of any doubt, headings are included in the word count, as are quotations.)

Criteria & Marking:

Assessment Criteria and Standards are provided in the course Blackboard site.
assessments.submission_guidelines: The Research Proposal should be submitted by email directly to your supervisor AND electronically on the Blackboard site.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
An in-person oral examination of the research paper, of approximately 30 minutes. This is a hurdle such that the student must pass the oral examination to pass the course.

The main objectives of the oral examination are to:

  • establish that the student fully understands the work and its wider implications;
  • provide the student with an opportunity to reply to criticism or challenge;
  • enable the examiner(s) to clarify issues in the research paper which may be unclear; and
  • validate the contribution made by the student to the research paper.

The oral examination will include assessment of the student’s ability to:

  • demonstrate detailed knowledge of the research paper;
  • locate their research in the broader context of their discipline;
  • demonstrate the originality of the thesis and the contribution it makes to state of knowledge in the field;
  • defend the methodology and conclusions of the thesis; and
  • display awareness of the limitations of the research.

Assessment Criteria and Standards are provided in the course Blackboard site.

The oral examination will be conducted by an Examiner who is a member of the academic staff of the Law School, but who is not the supervisor.

This examination will be recorded.
